scope.summary: Implement the MetaHuman garment export package that bundles the promoted garment mesh with MetaHuman-specific skeletal binding data so MetaHuman Creator can re-size the garment automatically when body sliders are adjusted
acceptance_criteria: POST /tailor/garments/:id/export with format=metahuman produces a directory containing: (1) a USD or FBX mesh with MetaHuman-compatible skinning weights, (2) a MetaHuman import JSON manifest listing the garment slot, body region, and LOD paths, and (3) a seam-allowance-stripped OBJ of each 2D panel for MetaHuman Creator's pattern-resize algorithm

The package records source garment/body/profile hashes, exact target skeleton and importer versions, units/axis/LOD contracts, and a deterministic artifact manifest; missing or incompatible MetaHuman target data returns a typed fail-closed error rather than HTTP 501, a placeholder, or an implicit compatibility claim

Reimport qualification proves skin weights, garment slot and body-region mapping, LOD references, panel provenance, body-slider refit behavior, and deterministic round-trip against the version-pinned MetaHuman target profile

The UserManual documents the complete export, import, validation, troubleshooting, and recovery workflow; MT-446 consumes this package for its live EveryWear-equivalent delivery lane without introducing a second MetaHuman export authority
scope.risk_if_missed: Without this export path, garments authored in Tailor cannot round-trip to MetaHuman Creator for body-slider-driven resizing, requiring manual re-fit for each body variation. This is a critical gap for UE5 game and cinematic productions using MetaHuman as their character standard.

risks: Broad MT scope can hide multiple review targets.
Markdown MT lists may disagree with packet-declared active/next MT truth.
Receipt routing may target an old MT if contract identity is omitted.
minimum_controls: Exactly one primary proof target per MT unless the packet records why not.
MT identity must be stable and referenced by receipt correlation.
Generated projection drift must not wake Coder or Validator by itself.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Non-UI scope: behavior remains observable through typed Tailor state, receipts, captures, diagnostics, and TraceProjection; GUI projection is verified by the owning native-shell MT.

target_entries: Tailor UserManual > Publishing and DCC interchange

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: This MT owns authoritative, job, or external-tool lifecycle events and must project the same event_id, run_id, actor_id, and correlation_id from EventLedger into Flight Recorder.
This MT emits typed diagnostics through its owning command or job and inherits retention, health, and projection behavior from the shared diagnostics substrate.
The owning native shell or scheduled job supplies Palmistry coverage; this MT must preserve operation identity and recovery handles.

required_changes_before_execution: Added gui_obligation, user_manual_obligation, and HBR-INT-009 tier obligations from the current MT template without removing original scope.
Consume the signed technical refinement, canonical command/surface registries, classified HBR tiers, and task-oriented UserManual contract before execution.
